standard_prerequisites.name: The closure of a subset of a topological space as the intersection of the closed neighbourhoods, and openness of the translates x + M_lambda
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Elementary topology of topological modules, as recalled in the chapter's section on linearly topologized modules
standard_prerequisites.use: Justifies passing between the closure and the intersection of closed sets and the use of the translates of the open submodules as neighbourhoods of x.

core_obligations: Observe that each N + M_lambda is open, hence closed, so their intersection is closed (proof lines 929-931).
Assume x is not in the closure of N, so that some translate x + M_lambda misses N (proof lines 931-932).
Conclude that x is not in N + M_lambda, which gives the reverse inclusion (proof lines 932-933).
proof_roadmap: Point-avoidance argument for the reverse inclusion (proof lines 931-933).
difficulty_reason: For a linearly topologized module M over a topological ring R with a fundamental system of open submodules M_lambda and a submodule N, the lemma computes the closure of N as the intersection of the N + M_lambda (statement lines 921-927). The proof is displayed in both directions: each N + M_lambda is open hence closed, so the intersection is closed; and if x is not in the closure of N then some x + M_lambda misses N entirely, whence x is not in N + M_lambda (proof lines 929-933). The level is H2: a short but complete elementary argument, with the open-and-closed observation and the point-avoidance argument both written out.
